title: Cubic-Equivariant Neural Density Functional Theory for Three-Dimensional Lattice Fluids
authors: Jens Weimar, Martin Oettel, Alessandro Simon
abstract: We construct a neural classical density functional that acts directly on unrestricted three-dimensional density profiles. As a computationally tractable test bed, we consider parallel hard cubes of side length three on a simple cubic lattice. A fully convolutional network learns the one-body direct-correlation functional $c^{(1)}[ρ]$ from data obtained with grand-canonical Monte Carlo simulations in randomized external potentials. Complete profiles are used during both training and inference; a stochastic Bernoulli mask on the output sites makes full-profile training effective without explicitly extracting and storing overlapping local density windows. Averaging the first-layer kernels over all 48 rotations and reflections of the cubic point group additionally imposes exact cubic equivariance without data augmentation. We compare the learned functional with independent simulation data and with the lattice fundamental-measure functional of Lafuente and Cuesta. The neural functional markedly improves the homogeneous equation of state and the density profile at a planar hard wall. For the anisotropic pair distribution around a fixed particle, both functionals reproduce the principal packing shells, with their relative accuracy depending on crystallographic direction. These results demonstrate neural density-functional calculations on complete three-dimensional profiles while also identifying accurate full-dimensional training data, thermodynamic consistency, and structural correlations as the central challenges for extensions to continuum fluids.
summary: This paper introduces a novel Cubic-Equivariant Neural Density Functional Theory (DFT) designed to calculate properties of 3D lattice fluids. It trains a neural network on complete density profiles to approximate the one-body direct-correlation functional, enforcing cubic symmetry exactly. The results show that this neural approach significantly improves predictions for bulk thermodynamics and planar wall adsorption compared to existing methods.
main_problem: To develop a computationally tractable method for calculating equilibrium structure and thermodynamics by approximating the excess free-energy functional within Density Functional Theory (DFT).
main_result: The neural functional significantly improves the accuracy for the homogeneous equation of state and the density profile at a planar hard wall compared to existing methods.
method: A fully convolutional neural network is trained to learn the one-body direct-correlation functional $c^{(1)}[ho]$ directly from complete 3D density profiles, enforcing exact cubic equivariance via kernel projection.
model_or_system: The study models three-dimensional lattice fluids using parallel hard cubes on a simple cubic lattice. The framework is based on classical DFT, which approximates the many-body problem variationally.
key_observables: Homogeneous equation of state, density profile at a planar hard wall, and anisotropic pair distribution around a fixed particle.
important_parameters: Packing fractions ($\eta$) ranging from $\approx 0.063$ to $0.6$; the cubic point group symmetry ($G=O_h$).
main_assumptions: The method is restricted to enforcing only discrete cubic lattice symmetry, and obtaining smooth 3D histograms for reliable training targets remains a bottleneck for continuum fluids.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the planar hard-wall packing-fraction profile ($\eta(z)$) comparison between neural and LC functionals, and volume renderings of the test-particle pair distribution $g(\mathbf{r})$ in various crystallographic directions ([100], [110], [111]).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the DFT framework, details the construction of the cubic-equivariant neural functional using GCMC data for training, compares its predictions (equation of state, wall profiles) against established functionals (Lafuente-Cuesta), and discusses limitations regarding continuum extension.
why_interesting: While focused on classical lattice fluids, the use of equivariant neural networks to enforce fundamental symmetries in a many-body functional is highly relevant for developing machine learning potentials or force fields applicable to quantum systems where symmetry constraints are paramount.
